aimarage: Your website needs the Aimarage Blog API, e.g. the small PHP blog aimarage-blog: https://github.com/Aimarage/aimarage-blog
Create a long random token, store only its SHA-256 hash on the server and enter the token here.
Enter the API address, e.g. https://your-site.com/blog/api. All languages your website offers are published, others are skipped. Discarding a published task withdraws the article.
wordpress: Log in to WordPress, go to Users > Profile.
At the bottom under "Application Passwords" enter a name (e.g. Aimarage) and click "Add New Application Password".
Enter the password shown here, plus your WordPress username and your website address.
webflow: In Webflow: Site settings > Apps & Integrations > API access > "Generate API token", scope CMS: read and write.
In the Designer open your blog collection under CMS, collection settings: copy the collection ID.
Check the field names (field slugs): title usually "name", address "slug", text "post-body".
git: GitHub: under Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens, create a token for this repo only with "Contents: Read and write" (Metadata: Read is added automatically). Aimarage needs nothing more.

GitLab: in the project under Settings > Access tokens, create a Project Access Token with role Developer (Maintainer if the branch is protected) and scope api. write_repository alone is not enough because Aimarage commits through the API.
Enter repo, branch and folder. File name with {'{'}slug{'}'}, {'{'}date{'}'} and {'{'}lang{'}'}, e.g. {'{'}slug{'}'}.md or {'{'}lang{'}'}/{'{'}slug{'}'}.md. Aimarage only writes into this folder.
Public address with the same placeholders, e.g. https://example.com/{'{'}lang{'}'}/blog/{'{'}slug{'}'}. After the commit, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel or Netlify rebuild the site.

publish.oneLang: The main language of the article is published. The featured image is the first image of the draft (WordPress only).
publish.gitLangs: Each language of the article becomes its own file. Without {'{'}lang{'}'} in the file name, translations get the language appended (e.g. article.en.md). A new version updates the same file. An image is only included with an image folder, taken from the first image of the draft (public/ and static/ are dropped from the address).
publish.gitSite: Your site has to read Markdown files from this folder as blog pages. Tell your Claude:
publish.gitPrompt: Set up a blog that reads Markdown files with this frontmatter from {dir}.
publish.gitFormat:
---
title: "Article title"
description: "Short description, up to 160 characters"
date: 2026-10-27          # first published
updated: 2026-10-27       # last change
slug: "article-title"
lang: en
translationKey: "article-title"   # same in all languages of an article
image: "/images/blog/image-1a2b3c4d5e.jpg"   # only if the article has an image
canonical: "https://example.com/en/blog/article-title"
draft: true               # only with "create as draft only"
ai_generated: true        # AI label under Art. 50 EU AI Act
---

Text in Markdown (## subheadings, lists, links), without a top-level heading.

bluesky: In Bluesky: Settings > Privacy and security > App passwords (link below).
"Add app password", name e.g. Aimarage, do not allow direct messages.
Enter handle and the shown password here, "Connect".
mastodon: On your instance: Preferences > Development > New application.
Name Aimarage, scopes only: write:statuses, write:media, read:accounts. Save.
Open the application, copy "Your access token" and enter it here with the instance address.
meta: Instagram must be a business or creator account linked to a Facebook page (Instagram > Settings > Account type).
developers.facebook.com > My apps > Create app > use case for Instagram and Facebook pages / Facebook Login for Business. Development mode is enough, you are admin.
Facebook Login > Settings > Valid OAuth redirect URIs: enter the address below.
App settings > Basic: enter app ID and app secret here, save.
Then in the project under Accounts click "Connect" at Instagram: Facebook asks for pages and Instagram account, tick all relevant ones.
instagram: Switch Instagram to a business or creator account (Instagram > Settings > Account type and tools). No Facebook page needed.
developers.facebook.com > My apps: open or create a Meta app and add the use case "Manage messaging and content on Instagram". Development mode is enough.

In the app: Instagram > API setup with Instagram login. Add the Instagram account as Instagram tester (App roles > Roles) and accept the invite in Instagram (Settings > Website permissions > Apps and websites > Tester invites).
Step "3. Set up Instagram business login" > Business login settings: add the address below to the OAuth redirect URIs, character for character. Meta requires https.
The same place shows the Instagram app ID and Instagram app secret (not the Facebook app ID). Enter both here and save.
Then in the project under Accounts click "Log in with Instagram" at Instagram. If the page does not load afterwards: copy the full address from the address bar into the field below.
Posting needs a JPG image or a video that is publicly reachable (Aimarage on a server). Access lasts 60 days and is renewed automatically every day.
threads: In the same Meta app add the use case "Access the Threads API" (own Threads app ID).
Under Threads > Settings enter the redirect address (Threads requires https; otherwise use your website address and paste below).
Enter Threads app ID and secret here, save, then connect in the project under Accounts.
linkedin: linkedin.com/developers > Create app (needs a company page as owner).
Products: add "Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect" and "Share on LinkedIn".
Auth > Authorized redirect URLs: enter the address below.
Enter client ID and secret here, save, then connect in the project under Accounts. Access lasts 60 days.
x: Once: create a developer account on developer.x.com, create project and app and add pay-per-use credits (about $0.015 per post, about $0.20 with a link).
App > User authentication settings: app permissions "Read and write", type of app "Web App, Automated App or Bot", callback URI = redirect address below, enter a website address.
Keys and tokens > OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret: enter both here, save.
Then click "Sign in with X" at X in the project under Accounts. This one app can connect any number of X accounts.
If X rejects "localhost": enter http://127.0.0.1:3210/api/connect/x/callback at X and here, and after authorizing paste the address from the address bar into the field below "Sign in with X".
tiktok: developers.tiktok.com > your app (Login Kit + Content Posting API).
Enter client key and secret here. The redirect address must exactly match the one in the app (https).
Connect in the project under Accounts, approve on TikTok. If the browser lands on your site (e.g. tonebase.com), copy the whole address and paste it there.
Videos only. Without an audited app, posts are private.
reddit: Optional, read only: Reddit hardly grants new API access anymore, Brave Search is enough. Posting on Reddit stays manual.
reddit.com/prefs/apps > "create another app" > type "script" (or "web app"), name e.g. Aimarage, redirect URI does not matter (e.g. http://localhost:3210).
Enter the ID below the app name and the secret here, plus your Reddit username. Save.
brave: The agent uses it to find current Reddit and forum posts itself. Posting stays manual.

why.waitDay: On other days it counts as self-promotion there and gets removed.
why.later: You'll get it to review then.
why.sweep: You then only copy the reply into the thread. If nothing fits today, there is nothing for you to do.
why.assign: Without an owner it just sits there.
why.selfDirectory: A listing brings a lasting link and visitors.
why.selfCommunity: Helpful replies from you build trust - no bot can do that.
why.selfSocial: This only works from your own account.
why.account: Without an account nobody can post or submit there.

inbox.title: Mailbox
inbox.help: Incoming mail from the last 14 days. If a mail no longer needs a reply, tap Done - that only affects this mail. The category in the dropdown also applies to future mail from the sender.
inbox.doneHint: Only this mail: no reply needed any more
inbox.doneDropped: Marked as done - open reply task discarded.

sum.antwort: {n} needs a reply | {n} need a reply

inbox.noMailbox: No mailbox set up for this project (Accounts > Mailbox).
inbox.empty: No mail in the last 14 days.
inbox.saved: Saved - applies to this sender from now on.
inbox.markSeen: Mark newsletters and ads as read
inbox.markSeenHint: Plain notifications too. Mail that needs a reply or is important stays unread. Nothing is deleted or moved.

mcpLog.title: Log of API and MCP calls
mcpLog.intro: Calls with your keys: time, key, program, tool, project, summary of the arguments (no contents) and result size. Kept for {n} days.
mcpLog.introAdmin: All calls in the workspace: time, key, person, program, tool, project, summary of the arguments (no contents) and result size. Kept for {n} days.
